I want to know! Did you use AI during the L.A. wildfires?

mattdpearce.substack.com/p/d…

Columbia Journalism Review (@CJR)

The LA Fires and what a disaster says about our physical and informational environments, by @Jon_Allsop. cjr.org/the_media_today/la_w…




— https://nitter.net/CJR/status/1878829345621659711#m

Matt Pearce 🦅🇺🇸 (@mattdpearce)

TAX ZUCKERBERG, FUND KICK-ASS LOCAL JOURNALISTS 

mattdpearce.substack.com/p/c…



— https://nitter.net/mattdpearce/status/1878607938547585212#m

TAX ZUCKERBERG, FUND KICK-ASS LOCAL JOURNALISTS 

mattdpearce.substack.com/p/c…
Lot of recalled products down there.

The feds keep eating shit in criminal court:

www.latimes.com/california/s...

It’s fun—a macabre sort of fun—this parlor game of “Who Goes AI?” And it simplifies things—asking the question in regard to specific journalists.

www.todayintabs.com/p/who-goes-ai
The extremely online journalist and content creator doesn’t believe in tech hygiene and yearns for a world where “inbox infinity” is celebrated. www.wired.com/story/user-b...
This is my approach these days tbh.

It’s getting easier to deal with internet news, I’m really zen about it but just have one move every time. Wrote your whole article with AI? Huh, must be for somebody else. Feminism-ending polycule? Guy is cutting in the bones in his face to look perfect? Hm, doesn’t have anything to do with me.

Journalists produce reliable information like bees produce honey - and our current age of AI is smashing the hive, killing the bees, and setting us up for total information collapse in the near future.

Great piece from @mattdpearce.com :

operator: 911, please state the nature of your emergency
me: there’s a site i go to a lot that isn’t the best way to follow breaking news
operator: is it a news site
me: not really
operator: why don’t you go to a news site
me: i don’t know
operator: jesus. ok. how many ambulances do you want
me: 75

Matt’s (correctly) laying out the bleak trajectory we’re on, but I would also say this exact scenario is why I’m optimistic about the future of independent news. Ppl need to get information from somewhere, and the backlash to AI and corporate media is only going to grow as the product deteriorates
eating the seed corn:
Thank you Paul! That’s very kind.
try and imagine a bigger W as an academic
This is a distressingly solid analogy 🐝🍯

Wherein I write about the step beyond Google Zero and imagine the AI information ecosystem collapse:

mattdpearce.substack.com/p/who-really...
You need to pay for news
When Baz Luhrman had the guns say "sword" on the side in Romeo + Juliet, that was the best choice that has been made in any modern adaptation ever.

Beyond the theft, the technology is absolutely there to capture sources for attribution.

That these companies lean toward obscuring sources is telling.
